newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs surge in post-election rally.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs surge in post-election rally.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures traded higher on Monday, as players covered their short positions after Japan's elections.
Dealers said the three-month interest rate futures were boosted by a rally in December JGBs, which established a new contract high of 123.72 on SIMEX.
"I heard Japanese trust banks were buying JGBs," said a dealer with a Japanese futures house.

Dealers said players covered their short JGB positions after a bout of profit-taking on the Nikkei, where expectations the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) would emerge with a majority had spurred strong buying last week.
December JGBs settled at 123.61 against their opening 122.90. "I'm looking at a target of 123.80 next and then the psychological 124.00 level," said a trader with a U.S. house.
He said the market also rose on comments by a Japanese Finance Ministry official who said there was no need for Japan to consider an extra stimulative budget at present.
The lead June Euroyen contract was quoted at 99.21 in late trade against its IMM close at 99.15. March finished at 99.35 against 99.31.
Eurodollar futures finished steady in thin trade as the market suffered from a lack of interest ahead of a week of sparse economic data.
"Eurodollars seem very well bid. It might be good to sell and book some profits at current levels," said a trader with a European institution.
He said the U.S. Treasury Department's two- and five-year note auctions were likely to provide the only lead this week.
"They may weigh on the market a little bit but sentiment is still bullish," he said.
March Eurodollars ended at 94.33 against their IMM close at 94.32. June were at 94.19 against 94.18.
